This is a short list of some common mathematical shapes and figures and the formulas that describe them.

== Two-dimensional shapes ==

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Shape !! [[Area]] !! Perimeter/Circumference !! Meanings of symbols
|-
|[[Square]]
|<math>l^2</math>
|<math>4l</math>
|<math>l</math> is the length of a side
|-
|[[Rectangle]]
|<math>lb</math>
|<math>2(l+b)</math>
|<math>l</math> is length, <math>b</math> is breadth
|-
|[[Circle]]
|<math>\pi r^2</math>
|<math>2\pi r</math> or <math>\pi d</math>
|where <math>r</math> is the radius and <math>d</math> is the diameter
|-
|[[Ellipse]]
|<math>\pi ab</math>
|
|where <math>a</math> is the [[semimajor axis]] and <math>b</math> is the [[semiminor axis]]
|-
|[[Triangle]]
|<math>\frac{bh}{2}</math>
|<math>a+b+c</math>
|<math>b</math> is base; <math>h</math> is height; <math>a,b,c</math> are sides
|-
|[[Parallelogram]]
|<math>bh</math>
|<math>2(a+b)</math>
|<math>b</math> is base, <math>h</math> is height, <math>a</math> is side
|-
|[[Trapezoid]]
|<math>\frac{a+b}{2}h</math>
|
|<math>a</math> and <math>b</math> are the bases
|}

This is a list of volume formulas of basic shapes:<ref name=":2">{{Cite book |last=Treese |first=Steven A. |title=History and Measurement of the Base and Derived Units |date=2018 |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]] |isbn=978-3-319-77577-7 |location=Cham, Switzerland |lccn=2018940415 |oclc=1036766223}}</ref>{{Rp|pages=405–406}}

* [[Cone]] – <math display="inline">\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h</math>, where <math display="inline">r</math> is the [[Base (geometry)|base]]'s radius and <math display="inline">h</math> is the cone's height;
* [[Cube]] – <math display="inline">a^3</math>, where <math display="inline">a</math> is the side's length;
* [[Cuboid]] – <math display="inline">abc</math>, where <math display="inline">a</math>, <math display="inline">b</math>, and <math display="inline">c</math> are the sides' length;
* [[Cylinder]] – <math display="inline">\pi r^2 h</math>, where <math display="inline">r</math> is the base's radius and <math display="inline">h</math> is the cylinder's height;
* [[Ellipsoid]] – <math display="inline">\frac{4}{3}\pi abc</math>, where <math display="inline">a</math>, <math display="inline">b</math>, and <math display="inline">c</math> are the [[semi-major and semi-minor axes]]' length;
* [[Sphere]] – <math display="inline">\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 </math>, where <math display="inline">r</math> is the radius;
* [[Parallelepiped]] – <math display="inline">abc\sqrt{K}</math>, where <math display="inline">a</math>, <math display="inline">b</math>, and <math display="inline">c</math> are the sides' length,<math display="inline">K = 1 + 2\cos(\alpha)\cos(\beta)\cos(\gamma) - \cos^2(\alpha) - \cos^2(\beta) - \cos^2(\gamma)</math>, and <math display="inline">\alpha</math>, <math display="inline">\beta</math>, and <math display="inline">\gamma</math> are angles between the two sides;
* [[Prism (geometry)|Prism]] – <math display="inline">Bh</math>, where <math display="inline">B</math> is the base's area and <math display="inline">h</math> is the prism's height;
* [[Pyramid (geometry)|Pyramid]] – <math display="inline">\frac{1}{3}Bh</math>, where <math display="inline">B</math> is the base's area and <math display="inline">h</math> is the pyramid's height;
* [[Tetrahedron]] – <math display="inline">{\sqrt{2}\over12}a^3</math>, where <math display="inline">a</math> is the side's length.

=== Sphere ===
{{See also|Volume of an n-ball|n-sphere#Volume and surface area}}

The basic quantities describing a sphere (meaning a [[n-sphere|2-sphere]], a 2-dimensional surface inside 3-dimensional space) will be denoted by the following variables
*<math>r</math> is the radius,
*<math>C = 2 \pi r</math> is the [[Circumference of a sphere|circumference]] (the length of any one of its [[great circle]]s),
*<math>S</math> is the [[surface area]],
*<math>V</math> is the [[volume]].

'''Surface area''':

<math display="block">\begin{alignat}{4}
S
&= 4 \pi r^2 \\[0.3ex]
&= \frac{1}{\pi} C^2 \\[0.3ex]
&= \sqrt[3]{\pi (6 V)^2} \\[0.3ex]
\end{alignat}</math>

'''Volume''':

<math display="block">\begin{alignat}{4}
V
&= \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \\[0.3ex]
&= \frac{1}{6 \pi^2} C^3 \\[0.3ex]
&= \frac{1}{6 \sqrt{\pi}} S^{3/2} \\[0.3ex]
\end{alignat}</math>

'''Radius''':

<math display="block">\begin{alignat}{4}
r
&= \frac{1}{2 \pi} C \\[0.3ex]
&= \sqrt{\frac{1}{4 \pi} S} \\[0.3ex]
&= \sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{4 \pi} V} \\[0.3ex]
\end{alignat}</math>

'''[[Circumference of a sphere|Circumference]]''':

<math display="block">\begin{alignat}{4}
C
&= 2 \pi r \\[0.3ex]
&= \sqrt{\pi S} \\[0.3ex]
&= \sqrt[3]{\pi^2 6 V} \\[0.3ex]
\end{alignat}</math>
